newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers profits up, Russia deal close.
newsitem.headline: De Beers profits up, Russia deal close.

text.p: Diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd posted sparkling year results on Tuesday and said that a deal with Russia on bringing the country back into its marketing cartel was close.
The firm's earnings per share rose to 354 U.S. cents from 259 cents and the group also increased its dividend by 10.5 percent to 102.7 U.S. cents a share.

Analysts had expected a good set of results following on from a good performance at the half year in August and record sales in 1996 by its Central Selling Organisation (CSO), which controls some 75 percent of the rough-diamond market.

The CSO has long dominated the market, but has been hit by the defection of the Argyle mine in Australia and the breakdown of a deal with Russia when that country missed a New Year's Eve deadline on signing a new agreement.
However, CSO managing director Gary Ralfe told a news conference that discussions had gone well during a trip to Russia three weeks ago.
"The process seems to be moving ahead satisfactorily following the suspension of the old agreement," he said.

Ralfe said he hoped to have a resolution soon signed by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin authorising the signing of a new agreement and a decree from President Boris Yeltsin that would make a modified memorandum of understanding signed in February 1996 a constitutional agreement.
"Things are moving ahead and we hope within the next couple of months to have those two final authorisations," he said.

Ralfe said it was important to bring the Russian federal government into the agreement to ensure that a deal breakdown did not happen again. He also suggested any new deal could be a rollover contract.
"The contract would not be an evergreen contract. It would be something that we could roll on quite easily," he said.
Ralfe declined to say what the modification to the memorandum of understanding would be. "The details of our agreement will remain confidential."
In its results statement De Beers said diamond demand remained strong, with good sales reported at the first two so-called "sights" of 1997, where the CSO sells to a select group of traders.
Market watchers say the firm is also reaping benefits from its investments in other firms like Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Minorco.
Total combined earnings, including the share of retained associates' earnings, were $1,344 million, up fom $986 million.
This included an exceptional profit of $109 million from the disposal of a portion of its interest in industrial holding firm Johnnic.
Excluding associates, earnings totalled $828 million against $624 million, while the diamond account for the year totalled $803 million compared to $760 million.
De Beers shares rose after the news was announced to a new year high of 159.75 cents before closing down 50 cents on the day at 157.00 on some profit-taking.
